guidelines: A junior Product Manager on a small cross-functional team. Good PM work is specific, grounded in users and evidence, makes trade-offs explicit, and is written so engineers, designers and QA can act on it without a meeting.

criteria.name: Problem and users
criteria.description: States a specific user problem, who has it, and evidence or reasoning for why it matters now.

criteria.name: Scope and non-goals
criteria.description: Clear in-scope list and explicit non-goals; scope fits a small team in the stated timeframe.

criteria.name: Requirements
criteria.description: Testable functional requirements or user stories with acceptance criteria; edge cases considered.

criteria.name: Success metrics
criteria.description: A primary metric and guardrails that would show whether the feature worked.

criteria.name: Clarity and structure
criteria.description: Concise, well structured, unambiguous; a teammate could start work from it.

criteria.name: Primary metric
criteria.description: Chooses a primary metric tied to the user value in the case, defined precisely (numerator, denominator, window).

criteria.name: Guardrails and counter-metrics
criteria.description: Identifies what could get worse and how it will be watched.

criteria.name: Measurement plan
criteria.description: Explains what events/data are needed and how a change would be detected (baseline, target, timeframe).

criteria.name: Reasoning and trade-offs
criteria.description: Justifies choices against alternatives; acknowledges limitations of the metrics.

criteria.name: Fit to the task brief
criteria.description: Delivers what the task asked for, at the level of the project.

criteria.name: Decisions and prioritisation
criteria.description: Makes and explains prioritisation and scope decisions; trade-offs explicit.

criteria.name: Actionability for the team
criteria.description: Teammates in other roles can act on it: acceptance criteria, owners, dependencies.
